sources.title: Use of continuous cranial shape variation in the identification of divergent crocodile species of the genus Mecistops
sources.scope: Comparison of adult cranial shape and linear measurements in the two living slender-snouted crocodiles; supports skull-shape differentiation and diagnostic variables, not ecological, population-size or range conclusions.
sources.attribution: Carr AN et al. (2021). Use of continuous cranial shape variation in the identification of divergent crocodile species of the genus Mecistops. Journal of Morphology 282(8):1219–1232. DOI 10.1002/jmor.21365. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The study found cranial-shape differences between the two living Mecistops species and identified nasal shape and snout length-to-width ratio at the premaxillary notch as especially informative.
claims.scope: Adult skull morphology and the study's measurement design; not a complete ecological account or an age-independent field key.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study does not establish population abundance, current conservation status, or complete range-wide morphological variation.
